The family crypt at {place} goes deeper than the family remembers. Explore it, quietly.
details: The site is an old smugglers' warren with false walls and a dozen crawlspaces; mapping it fully takes three days.
The structure predates the city and is built of black stone that drinks light; torches illuminate only half their usual radius.
A colony of {monster} has made a home in the lower levels and defends it fiercely.
A lost team of Iron-rank adventurers is still inside, trapped behind a collapsed passage.
The site contains a sealed vault with a magical lock that needs a DC 15 Intelligence (Arcana) check to understand.
The ruins flood with each high tide, and the team has only six hours between floods.
The ruins are older than any known kingdom, and their carvings show essence users of a kind nobody recognises.
Air in the deeper passages is stale; without fresh air, characters make Constitution saves each hour.
A previous explorer left a journal on the first level, describing everything until the last page.
The site has natural light from glowing fungus, enough to see by but strange to read by.
There is a working door with a riddle on it, and the answer is written backwards on the inside.
Part of the site floods at high tide, and the timing must be judged carefully.
Local legend says the site is cursed; the actual danger is a colony of nesting monsters.
The site contains a shrine to a god no church now worships, and the gods have opinions about that.
Each level has a different magic level; spells work normally above and oddly below.
complications: The ceiling is unstable; loud noise or fire magic causes a collapse dealing 2d6 bludgeoning damage, DC 14 Dexterity save for half.
Air in the deeper tunnels is foul; each hour requires a DC 12 Constitution save or gain a level of exhaustion.
A rival treasure hunter is already inside and has set traps for competitors.
The map the client provided is wrong in several important places.
Local villagers believe the place is cursed and will not sell supplies to anyone going there.
The team's light sources begin to flicker and fail as they go deeper.
Treasure hunters arrive the same day with a cart and a lot of rope.
A rockfall seals the way the team came in.
The client wants every find, however small, handed over unexamined.
A Magic Society rival team claims prior rights to the site.
The monsters inside are territorial and know every shortcut.
The map the client provided is wrong in one crucial place.
Local villagers believe disturbing the site will bring disaster and try to stop the team.
A hidden astral space opens when the team touches the wrong stone.
Strange weather strikes the moment the team enters, and doesn't stop.
twists: The site was sealed on purpose by an old order of priests, and opening it has woken what they buried.
The client already knows what is inside and wants proof it exists before buying the land cheaply.
The lost expedition did not die; they found something valuable and are hiding from their own employer.
The place is the dormant entrance to an astral space that has not yet fully opened.
Everything inside has been explored before; the old maps were stolen and suppressed by {faction}.
The site is not abandoned: a small, frightened community lives in its deepest part.
Exploring the site wakes something that was sleeping and better left so.
The site is an old cult temple, and the cult still visits on holy days.
The lost tower is a prison, and its prisoner is still alive.
The client is descended from the people who built the site and wants it buried, not mapped.
The explorer who went missing eighty years ago is inside, unaged.
The ruins are where an early outworlder landed, and their notes are still there.
proof: A complete map of the site, accepted by the Society cartographer
Copies of any inscriptions or ward patterns found
A sample object from the deepest point reached
A map of the site, signed by every team member
Rubbings or sketches of the most important inscriptions
One recovered object, logged and handed over at the counter

types.label: Defence
notices: Defenders needed. {count} {monster} have been testing the palisade at {place} every night. Hold the walls for {days} days until the garrison returns.
{client} requires protection. Threats have been made by {faction}. Guard the household at {place} until the danger passes.
Village under siege. {place} cannot hold another raid. Anyone who can fight, come now. Ask for {npc}.
Military order: reinforce the watchtower at {place} against {monster} incursions. Report to the sergeant on duty. Rotation: {days} days.
Bodyguard contract. {npc}, a witness in an upcoming trial, must be kept alive in {place} until the hearing. Discretion essential.
The orchard at {place} is being stripped every night by {monster}. Defend the harvest until the picking is done. Posted for {client}.
we built our church with our own hands and something keeps tearing down the walls. {place}, the little one by the stream. we can feed you and pray for you. ask for {npc}.
Society contract. Defend the Magic Society field station at {place} during a ritual lasting {days} days. Disturbances must be prevented at all costs.
Defend the farmsteads at {place} through the next {days} nights. Something comes out of the woods after dark and tests the fences.
{client} needs guards on the walls of {place} while the militia is away. The walls are short. Be tall.
Help needed to hold the bridge at {place} against {monster} until the floodwater drops.
The Society needs a team at {place} while the town's protectors are recovering from injuries. Expect {count} attacks.
Hold the watchtower on the pass above {place} until relieved. Relief has been due for a week.
Defend the vineyard at {place} through the harvest. Last year, {monster} ate the grapes, the pickers and the cart.
The orphanage at {place} has received threats. Watch it, and the children, for {days} days.
Protect the excavation at {place} while the Magic Society works. Diggers keep vanishing. Do better.
{place} has a monster surge coming, or so the Magic Society says. Help the town prepare and stand with it.
Defend the lighthouse at {place} for the storm season. Whoever lights it gets attacked. Someone must light it.
Guard the granary at {place} through the winter; rats the size of dogs keep trying to get in. Rats, plural.
Shepherds at {place} need protection during lambing. {monster} are drawn to the new lambs.
details: The attackers come at the same hour every night, just after moonrise, always from the east side.
The village's defences are rotten; with a day's work and a DC 13 check with carpenter's tools, the team can rebuild a section.
The threat is real but smaller than claimed; the client panicked and exaggerated the danger.
The villagers will fight but have only pitchforks and courage; organising them is possible with a DC 14 Charisma (Persuasion) check.
There is only one gate, but a forgotten drainage tunnel lets attackers in under the wall.
The protected person refuses to stay indoors and insists on keeping their normal routine.
The defenders have one working ballista, and nobody knows how to aim it.
The attacks follow a pattern: three nights quiet, then one night of fury.
The settlement has a healer, but she's a child of twelve with a borrowed divine essence.
There is a secret tunnel into the settlement, and the attackers know about it.
The town has stockpiled oil and has never once used it in a defence.
The walls are in good repair on the side facing the road and badly broken on the side facing the forest.
The militia captain has been bribed to sleep through the third night.
Torches and bonfires keep the monsters away, but the firewood runs out on the fifth night.
The townsfolk are eager to help and slightly worse than useless.
complications: The attackers grow bolder each night and on the last night come in force.
Someone inside the defended place is opening the gate for the enemy.
The garrison that should relieve the team is delayed by a week.
Supplies run low halfway through, and the client cannot afford more.
Fire arrows set the thatched roofs alight during the second attack.
The protected person is hated by half the town and the team must defend them from neighbours too.
The town council argues about everything, including where the team may stand.
A sickness spreads among the defenders midway through.
One attack comes from an entirely unexpected direction: underground, the river or the sky.
A noble demands half the team guard his house instead of the walls.
Refugees from a nearby village arrive mid-siege and need to be let in.
Someone inside the settlement is signalling the attackers.
The well is poisoned on the second day.
A storm blows out every torch on the walls at once.
The attackers bring something new on the last night: a leader.
twists: The monsters are drawn by a cursed object buried under the village well.
The client is guilty of the crime the threatening faction accuses them of.
The attacks are a distraction while {faction} robs a different target nearby.
The creatures are not attacking; they are trying to reach their stolen young held in a barn.
The garrison commander abandoned the post deliberately and is now selling the region's safety to the highest bidder.
The monsters are fleeing toward the settlement, not attacking it; something worse is behind them.
The attackers are the settlement's own lost children, changed by an astral space.
The town is defending stolen goods, and the attackers are trying to get them back.
A cult is steering the attacks to force the town to abandon a sacred site.
The defence is a distraction while the client empties the town treasury.
The monster leader can talk, and it is willing to bargain.
The threat was invented by the town council to get Society help for free repairs.
proof: The defended site or person is intact when the contract period ends
Signed statement from the client or garrison officer
Bodies or cores of the attackers, if any were killed
The settlement still stands and the elders sign to say so
Cores from the attackers, counted at the counter
Testimony from the relieving garrison

types.label: Retrieval
notices: Lost: {item}. Last seen near {place}. {client} offers payment for its return, no questions asked.
Retrieval contract. {item} was stolen from the Society vault and is believed to be in {place}. Recover it intact.
{client} desires the recovery of {item}, lost when a cart overturned in the river near {place}. The current is strong. Divers preferred.
Find {item}. It was taken by {faction} three days ago from a house in {place}. Get it back before they sell it.
My father's {item} was buried with him, and grave robbers have dug him up. Please bring it back. He is in the churchyard at {place}. {npc} knows more.
Item recovery. {item} was dropped by a fleeing adventurer inside a {monster} lair near {place}. Lair remains active.
To any honest company: {item} has been taken from my household at {place}. I suspect a servant. The matter must not reach the magistrate. Signed, {client}.
The Magic Society requires recovery of {item}, last carried by {npc} into the hills above {place}. Researcher missing. Item takes priority.
Recover {item}, lost when a cart went off the cliff road near {place}. The cart can stay. The item cannot.
{client} seeks the return of {item}, taken by {monster} to their nest near {place}.
Lost: {item}. Last seen at an inn in {place} the night of the fight. Finder's fee for return, more for names.
Retrieve {item} from the sunken barge in the river at {place}. Swimmers needed. Eels present.
Recover the bell stolen from the temple at {place}. The thieves can't ring it. Nobody can, without the clapper.
Society contract: retrieve the gear of a fallen team from the astral space near {place}. Their families want it back.
{item} was buried with a man who did not own it. Retrieve it from the cemetery at {place}. With the family's permission.
Find and return {count} runaway prize hens from the woods near {place}. They are worth more than they look. Much more.
Recover {item} from the pawnshop in {place} before the pawnbroker realises what it is.
Retrieve the signal mirror from the old watchtower above {place}. It was moved. The tower was not.
The library at {place} wants a book back. It was borrowed in good faith eleven years ago. Find the borrower.
A child's toy fell into the well at {place}. The child insists. The well is much deeper than it should be.
details: The item has already changed hands twice and now sits in a pawnshop in {place}, priced at triple its value.
A magpie-like {monster} took the item and keeps it in a nest high in a dead tree with other shiny objects.
The thief is a desperate youth who sold it to pay for medicine; the buyer is a dangerous collector.
The item lies at the bottom of a flooded cellar, requiring DC 13 Strength (Athletics) checks to dive for it.
There are three copies of the item in circulation, and only one is genuine; a DC 14 Intelligence (Investigation) check spots the forgery.
The item was broken in two, and each half is now held by a different person.
The item has been sold twice already, and each buyer knows the next.
The item is hidden in plain sight, set into the wall of a building as decoration.
The thief left behind a single glove with a crest on it.
The item gives off a faint chime that can be followed with a DC 13 Wisdom (Perception) check.
The lair where it's held is reached only at low tide.
The item has been broken in two, and the halves are in different places.
A fence in the city has the item and wants to bargain for it.
The item is valuable to the monster that took it; it's lining its nest.
There is a replica, and the client cannot tell the difference without an appraiser.
complications: The current holder believes they bought it legally and has a receipt to prove it.
The item is warded, and anyone who touches it bare-handed takes 2d6 psychic damage.
The local watch is also looking for the item and suspects the team of the original theft.
{faction} has put a bounty on whoever recovers it first.
The item is hidden in a public place, a temple's offering vault, where violence would be sacrilege.
The client keeps adding conditions about how the item must be returned.
The current holder believes, honestly, that the item is rightfully theirs.
Taking the item back is legal only with a magistrate's writ, which takes three days.
Another team was hired to retrieve the same item by someone else.
The item is trapped by its last owner, who did not want it taken.
The item is in a temple, and a priest guards it.
The thieves are children who stole it for a reason.
The item has bonded to someone who now cannot let it go.
Removing the item collapses the structure around it.
The item draws the attention of a monster as soon as it is moved.
twists: The item was never stolen; the client hid it and wants to claim the loss from a debt collector.
The item is a key to something much more valuable, and the client has not said what.
The supposed thief is the item's true owner, taking back what was stolen from them years ago.
The item has a minor curse that makes its keeper paranoid, which explains the client's odd behaviour.
The Magic Society researcher faked their own disappearance to sell the item to a rival.
The item is the client's stolen property, but the client stole it first.
The item contains a trapped spirit that asks the team to set it free.
The item is a forgery, and the real one was never lost.
Someone wants the item lost forever because it proves a crime.
The item is one of a set, and putting the set together does something.
The thief is an old friend of one of the team members.
The item is sought by a cult, which will follow the team home.
proof: The item itself, handed over at the Society counter
Identification of the item by the client's mark or seal
A sworn statement of where and from whom it was recovered
The item itself, handed to the client in person
The client's receipt, witnessed at the counter
A full account of where the item was found, for the Society's records

types.label: Astral Space Clearance
notices: Society Notice: a new astral space, designated {astral}, has opened near {place}. Clear it, reach the heart and close it. Bronze rank recommended.
Astral clearance contract. The portal to {astral} outside {place} has been charted but not cleared. Teams may keep loot not claimed by the Society.
Urgent: the astral space {astral} near {place} is showing signs of instability. Clear and close within {days} days or risk a monster surge.
{client} owns the land where {astral} has appeared near {place} and wishes it closed before it frightens the tenants. Society terms apply.
Military order: the {astral} portal at {place} must be sealed before troops move through the area. Clear all hostiles. Report to {npc}.
Magic Society research request: enter {astral} near {place}, record its rules and environment, and close it only after observation is complete.
Our children found a glowing door in the hill above {place}. something came out of it. the Society man called it {astral}. please close it.
Society contract: a team that entered {astral} near {place} has not returned. Clear the space, recover survivors and close the portal.
Clear the astral space {astral} near {place} before the nearby village loses any more goats. Or children.
Twin portals near {place} lead to the same astral space, {astral}. Go in one, come out the other. Close both.
{client} has bought the rights to the astral space {astral} near {place} and needs it cleared before his own people go in.
The astral space {astral} near {place} keeps reopening after it's closed. Find out why.
Iron-rank clearance: a small space, {astral}, near {place}. Good first contract. Mind the traps.
Escort a Magic Society scholar into {astral} near {place} and keep her alive while she studies the walls.
{astral}, near {place}, is the largest space opened in years. Several teams needed. Coordinate at the counter.
The astral space {astral} near {place} has started leaking its weather into the real world. It's snowing in summer.
Clear {astral} near {place}, and bring back the heart's reward intact. {client} has already sold it.
Retrieve the body of a Society member from {astral} near {place}. The family wants a burial.
The astral space {astral} near {place} has a rule nobody has worked out. Three teams failed. Be the fourth.
Clear {astral} near {place} within {days} days. The Society has a waiting list of teams who'd love the cores.
details: The space is small, only three chambers and a heart, but each chamber is guarded by {count} {monster}.
Time runs differently inside; each hour in the space is roughly ten minutes outside.
The heart holds a guardian that regenerates unless its anchor stone is broken first.
Previous visitors left chalk marks on the walls, some of them deliberately misleading.
The portal is shrinking, and the team has a day or two before it closes with anyone still inside.
The space shifts slightly each time someone enters, so the Society's preliminary map is only partly accurate.
The space's rule forbids speech; anyone who speaks takes psychic damage.
Each chamber reflects the fears of the person who enters first.
The space is a maze that resets every hour.
There is a friendly inhabitant, a spirit who trades knowledge for stories.
The guardian is vulnerable only to the affinity the space rejects.
The space's monsters drop extra cores but corrode weapons.
There's a rest point halfway through, guarded by a puzzle.
A previous team's gear lies scattered, with notes on what killed them.
The heart reward is chosen from three, and the space remembers who chose.
complications: Another team has already entered and is looting the outer chambers ahead of the party.
The space rejects one affinity entirely; powers tied to it deal half damage inside.
A Magic Society observer insists on accompanying the team and taking notes at the worst moments.
The landowner demands a share of any loot as rent.
Monsters inside are smarter than expected and set ambushes at narrow passages.
Closing the space requires holding a ritual circle for one minute while the heart's guardians attack.
The portal starts shrinking faster than predicted.
One team member is trapped by the space's rule.
A rival team is inside and has made a deal with the guardian.
The space's monsters follow the team back through the portal.
The space is larger than its outside suggested.
An astral being takes interest in one of the team.
The space has two hearts, and closing one opens the other.
The space shifts the team's essences, temporarily changing their powers.
The scholar insists on studying something dangerous.
twists: The astral space was opened deliberately by {faction}, who are using it to farm monster cores.
The missing team found a second, deeper space within the first and are trapped in it.
The heart's treasure is a tool that could open new astral spaces, and several parties want it.
The space is tied to someone's dreams, and the client is that dreamer.
The monsters inside are fleeing something worse that has not yet reached the heart.
The space is a prison built to hold something, and clearing it frees the prisoner.
The space was created by a dead god and contains a fragment of their power.
The space is linked to another space on the far side of the world.
The guardian is the ghost of an adventurer who died here, and wants release.
The space is being farmed by a noble house, which wants it left open.
The heart reward is an awakening stone of a kind never seen before.
The space is a test set by an astral being, and passing it earns its notice.
proof: The portal is closed and confirmed by a Society inspector
The heart guardian's core
A written report of the space's rules and layout
The portal closed, confirmed by a Society inspector
The guardian's core, checked at the counter
A map of the space for the Society's archive

types.label: Investigation
notices: Investigator wanted. Livestock in {place} found drained of blood. {client} wants to know what is responsible before it moves on to people.
Discreet inquiries required. {npc} has gone missing from {place} and the family suspects {faction}. Report findings only to the client.
Society Investigation: several adventurers have reported equipment theft at the Society lodge in {place}. Identify the culprit within {days} days.
Something is poisoning the wells of {place}. Find out who or what, and stop it. Posted for {client}.
To discreet persons of quality: a matter of family honour in {place} requires gentle investigation. Inquire with my steward, {npc}. Signed, {client}.
Strange singing comes from the cemetery at {place} every night. The church wants to know why. {monster} tracks reported.
The Magic Society requests investigation of unexplained magical surges in {place}. Possible connection to an unregistered astral space. Contact {npc} on arrival.
my husband says he goes fishing but he comes back every night soaked in something that isn't water. we live in {place}. {npc} says you can help.
Investigate the deaths of {count} cattle at {place}. No wounds. No sickness. Eyes all turned white. Find the cause.
{client} believes a servant is stealing from the household at {place}. Find out who, quietly, without upsetting the staff.
Strange lights over the marsh at {place} every night for a week. The Magic Society would like an explanation that isn't 'ghosts'.
Three Iron-rankers have quit the Society in {place} this month and none will say why. Find out.
The well at {place} sings at midnight. The villagers want it to stop. The priest wants to know what it's singing.
Investigate missing persons in the dock district of {place}. Four gone in a tenday. The watch has given up.
Someone is leaving carved wooden birds on doorsteps in {place}, and every house that gets one has a death within the month.
A Society clerk at {place} is suspected of selling contracts to favoured teams. Gather proof. Do not get caught gathering it.
Find out why the essence prices at the {place} market jumped overnight. {client} smells a ring.
Monsters near {place} are behaving oddly: travelling in pairs, avoiding roads, ignoring easy prey. Explain this.
{npc} swears her husband came home from the war a different man. Literally. Investigate, with tact.
The magistrate of {place} wants an outside eye on a murder everyone thinks is solved.
details: The culprit is a jealous neighbour using a crude alchemical poison; a DC 13 Wisdom (Medicine) check identifies it.
The trail leads to a hidden cellar beneath a tavern where {faction} meets twice a week.
A witness saw everything but will only talk after the team helps fix her broken cart wheel.
The evidence points at an obvious suspect, but a DC 15 Intelligence (Investigation) check reveals it was planted.
The events follow a pattern linked to the phases of the moon.
The local constable is lazy rather than corrupt and will help if flattered.
Every victim visited the same bathhouse in the week before they vanished.
The clues point to a respected Church of Truth priest, who is innocent and furious about it.
A street child saw everything and will talk for a hot meal and a promise.
The obvious suspect has an alibi that only holds up if a clock was wrong.
A key witness speaks only an old dialect; someone with the right language or a Society translator is needed.
The crime scene has been cleaned, badly; a DC 14 Intelligence (Investigation) check finds what was missed.
Ledgers show payments to a name that appears nowhere else in the city.
The trail leads to a noble house, which closes its doors as soon as the team arrives.
A pattern on the map shows the incidents form a circle, and the centre is somewhere nobody looks.
complications: The town distrusts outsiders, and interviews require a DC 14 Charisma check or the subject refuses to talk.
A second incident happens while the team is in town, making them suspects.
The client keeps interfering with the investigation to steer it away from certain people.
Key evidence is burned in a fire on the second night.
The local gossip sheet prints the team's suspicions before they have proof.
Interfering with the culprit draws the attention of a much more powerful enemy.
The watch captain resents outsiders and arrests a team member on a pretext.
The main witness disappears the night before they were due to talk.
A gossip sheet publishes the team's suspicions before they have proof.
The client starts hiding things once the investigation gets close to home.
A second crime happens that seems connected and isn't.
The guilty party learns of the investigation and starts planting false clues.
The investigation offends a powerful church, which demands it stop.
A key document is written in a cipher.
The evidence points at one of the team's own allies.
twists: The client is the culprit and hired the team to learn how much others know.
The strange events are caused by a frightened young person whose magic is awakening without training.
The missing person is alive and fled willingly from an abusive household.
Two unrelated crimes are happening at the same time, and the clues are tangled together.
The culprit is a monster that has learned to mimic a respected townsperson.
The culprit is a monster that has learned to wear a human face.
The deaths are mercy killings, carried out at the victims' own request.
The client is the guilty party and hired the team to find a scapegoat.
Two separate criminals are at work, each covering for the other by accident.
The victims are not dead but taken into an astral space, and some can still be saved.
A cult is behind it, and its leader sits on the town council.
The investigation was set up by an old enemy of the team, to draw them out.
proof: A written report naming the cause, accepted by the client
Physical evidence of the culprit's involvement
A confession or the culprit delivered to the authorities
A written report naming the culprit, with evidence
The culprit, delivered to the watch
A confession, witnessed by a priest of the Church of Truth

types.label: Rescue
notices: RESCUE NEEDED. {npc} was dragged off by {monster} near {place} last night. Every hour counts. Posted by {client}.
Society Contract: an Iron-rank team is overdue from a job near {place}. Locate them and bring them home. Last check-in was {days} days ago.
Miners trapped in a collapsed tunnel beneath {place}. Air is running out. {count} men are still down there. Anyone with strength or earth magic, come now.
{faction} has kidnapped the daughter of {client} and is holding her near {place}. They demand ransom. We demand her back without paying.
please. my little boy went into the woods by {place} after a glowing light and has not come back. {npc} saw something big moving out there.
Military order: a patrol of {count} soldiers is cut off by {monster} in the hills near {place}. Break through and extract survivors.
Humble request from the church at {place}: our pilgrims were taken by slavers on the old road. We cannot pay much. We beg your aid. {npc} saw which way they went.
Rescue contract. A fishing boat is stranded on a sandbar off {place}, and the {monster} are circling. Retrieve the crew.
RESCUE: a hunting party of {count} is overdue from the hills above {place}. Last seen three days ago. Every hour counts.
{client}'s daughter has been taken by {monster}. They went toward {place}. Bring her back. Pay is everything we have.
Miners trapped after a collapse at {place}. The Society needs a team who can dig and fight; something is in the tunnels with them.
A Bronze team entered the astral space at {place} and hasn't come out. The portal closes in {days} days.
Ransom note received. Pay or rescue. {client} prefers rescue. Kidnappers holding the hostage near {place}.
Rescue the crew of a fishing boat stranded on a rock off {place}. Tide's coming in.
Rescue the stranded villagers of {place}, cut off by floods, before the {monster} that live in the floodwater reach them.
A noble's hunting dogs got loose and chased a child into the woods near {place}. Find the child. The dogs are optional.
Pilgrims lost on the mountain path to {place}. Snow coming. Guide is among the lost.
Prisoners of bandits near {place}. Get them out. The bandits keep moving camp; {npc} knows where they were yesterday.
Someone fell down the old well at {place} and is still alive, and still talking. The voice says it's not alone.
An outworlder appeared in the swamp near {place}, frightened and confused. Bring them in before the swamp eats them.
details: The victims are held in an old barn three miles out, guarded by {count} poorly trained thugs.
The missing person is injured and hiding in a hollow tree, too frightened to call out; a DC 14 Wisdom (Perception) check spots them.
The monster that took the victim is keeping them alive as food for its young.
The trapped miners can be reached through an old ventilation shaft too narrow for armour.
Survivors are split into two groups, and saving both requires splitting the party.
The victims have been moved once already, and the trail goes cold at a river crossing.
The missing have left a trail of torn cloth, deliberately, every hundred yards.
The captives are being moved at night, and the rescuers must catch up by day.
One of the missing is injured, slowing any escape, and must be carried.
The kidnappers have hired a mage who can sense anyone approaching with magic.
The trapped people are in a pocket of air that will last about ten hours.
There are more captives than anyone reported, including people nobody was looking for.
The rescue site is reachable only by a rope bridge that holds two people at a time.
The captors have a Society badge and claim the right to hold their prisoners.
The captives are being fed something that makes them docile and unwilling to leave.
complications: One of the victims has a broken leg and must be carried out.
The kidnappers threaten to kill a hostage if they see armed adventurers.
A sudden storm floods the low ground and cuts off the escape route.
The rescued people are terrified and panic at the worst possible moment.
Another rescue party of villagers blunders in and gets captured too.
The victims' captors are themselves victims, forced by threats to their own families.
One of the rescued refuses to leave without something, or someone, left behind.
The kidnappers threaten to kill a hostage if they see anyone armed.
The rescuers are rescued themselves by someone who now wants a share of the reward.
A rival team gets there first and demands the credit.
Weather closes in and the way back is cut off for a day.
One captive is a known criminal the watch also wants.
Freeing the captives sets off an alarm, and their captors' allies come running.
The captive doesn't want to be rescued.
The people being rescued speak a language no one on the team knows.
twists: The rescued person does not want to go home and arranged their own disappearance.
The 'kidnapping' is a ransom scheme run by the victim and a lover.
The overdue team abandoned one of their own and has been hiding the truth.
The captors took the victims to protect them from a curse spreading in their village.
The person to be rescued is now infected with something the team will bring home with them.
The missing person staged their own disappearance to escape the client.
The captors were protecting the captives from something worse.
The rescue target is now a monster, partway through a transformation.
The rescued person is someone the team has met before, and not as a friend.
One of the hostages is the real leader of the kidnappers.
The rescue was arranged by the kidnappers to collect a second reward.
The captives have found something valuable in captivity and want to go back for it.
proof: The rescued people returned safely to the client
Their Society badges or tokens, if they are adventurers
Signed testimony from the survivors
The rescued, alive and returned to their families
A signed thanks from the client, witnessed at the counter
The rescued person's own account, given to the duty clerk

types.label: Bounty
notices: BOUNTY. {npc}, wanted for murder and arson in {place}. Bring them in alive for full payment. Reduced payment for proof of death.
Wanted by the magistrate of {place}: the leader of {faction}. Alive preferred. Considered armed and dangerous.
Bounty contract. {count} escaped prisoners fled toward {place} after breaking out of the garrison stockade. Return them in chains within {days} days.
{client} offers a private bounty on the swindler known as {npc}, last seen running a false relic stall in {place}.
Society Disciplinary Notice: former adventurer {npc} has broken their license oath and fled toward {place}. Capture and return for judgement.
Wanted dead or alive: the bandit captain who leads raids on the road to {place}. Rides with {count} men. Price set by the road wardens.
Bounty. A poacher keeps killing protected {monster} in the reserve near {place}. Catch them in the act. Posted by {client}.
He stole my savings and my sister's heart and ran off to {place}. His name is {npc}. I want him in front of a judge.
WANTED, alive: {npc}, for theft of Society property at {place}. Reward doubled if he hasn't spent it.
Bounty on the bandit leader called the Grey Hand, last seen near {place}. Dead or alive; alive pays more.
Wanted for desertion and murder: a former Iron-rank adventurer, last seen at {place}. Do not engage alone.
{client} offers a reward for the arsonist who burned the granary at {place}. Witnesses describe a limp and a red scarf.
WANTED: a counterfeiter flooding {place} with false spirit coins. The coins glow faintly. So, likely, do his hands.
Bounty posted by the Church of Justice: a confessed killer escaped the temple cells at {place}. Bring him back for judgement.
Wanted: a smuggler known only as the Heron, working the waterways around {place}. Proof of capture required.
Wanted for crimes against the dead: a grave robber who has struck three times at {place}. The families want him alive.
Bounty: the poacher killing protected stags on the duke's land near {place}. He's a good shot. Be better.
Wanted: the confidence trickster who sold {client} a fake essence at {place}. She is very charming. You were warned.
Rogue core user, Iron rank, attacking travellers on the road to {place}. Bounty paid by the road wardens.
Wanted by the Magic Society: an apprentice who fled {place} with {item}. Return both. The apprentice is optional.
details: The target hides in plain sight working as a cook at a roadside inn under a false name.
The fugitive has a network of friends in {place} who will warn them; a DC 14 Dexterity (Stealth) approach keeps surprise.
The target is Bronze rank and fights well, but has a bad knee that slows them after a few rounds.
The bandits shelter in an old fort with one entrance and a back way known only to a local shepherd.
The fugitive keeps a trained hound that barks at strangers.
The target has bought magical shackles that suppress capture spells, sewn into their coat.
The target has a sister in {place} who still sends him food.
The target is known to visit the same tavern every tenday, and the barkeep doesn't like him.
The target has changed his name twice; the third name is on a ship's manifest.
The target is protected by locals who think he's a hero.
The bounty poster's description is wrong in one important way.
The target has an awakening stone that lets him vanish once a day.
Another bounty hunter has the target's trail and is two days ahead.
The target has written to the Society asking for terms.
The target's crimes were committed under orders from a powerful patron.
complications: Another bounty hunter is closing in and is happy to steal the catch.
Locals protect the target because they once paid a village's debts.
The target surrenders easily and then tries to escape on the journey back.
The magistrate changes the terms to dead only, for reasons they will not give.
The fugitive takes a hostage when cornered.
The reward notice has been copied, and dozens of amateurs are blundering around looking for the target.
The target hides in a temple and claims sanctuary.
The target has taken a hostage.
A crowd forms to stop the arrest.
The target is sick and will die without care on the way back.
The bounty is withdrawn halfway through the hunt, without explanation.
The target offers the team more than the bounty to let him go.
The local watch claims jurisdiction and wants the target handed to them.
The target has an accomplice nobody knew about.
The target is wanted in two places, and both want him first.
twists: The target is innocent of the crime and has proof that would ruin a powerful family.
The bounty was posted by the target's own allies to lure hunters into an ambush.
The fugitive is a Society informant, and catching them would expose a larger operation.
The real criminal is the person who reported the crime.
The target is dying of a magical illness and only fled to find a cure.
The target is innocent, framed by the one who posted the bounty.
The target is a former member of a noble house, and the house wants him quietly dead.
The bounty poster wants the target alive to silence him somewhere else.
The target is a hidden outworlder who doesn't understand the crimes he's charged with.
The target is protecting a child who will be orphaned if he's taken.
Capturing the target uncovers a list of names the city's powerful would kill to recover.
The target is a cultist who wants to be caught, to be brought inside the walls.
proof: The target delivered alive to the named authority
The target's head, signet or distinctive tattoo for reduced payment
A sealed warrant stamped as executed by the magistrate
The target, delivered to the watch or the Society cells
The target's signet, weapon or other known possession
Witnessed death and burial, with a priest's signature

types.label: Gathering
notices: Gatherers needed. {client} requires {count} bundles of moonpetal from the meadows above {place}. Picked at night only.
The Magic Society seeks harvested parts from {monster} found near {place}: glands, scales and teeth, preserved in salt.
Gathering contract. Collect river pearls from the shallows near {place}. Beware the {monster} that nest there.
Herbalist needs fresh bloodroot from the bogs outside {place} within {days} days. Roots must be whole. Ask for {npc}.
Alchemical supply order: {count} jars of glowing cave moss from the caverns beneath {place}. Moss spoils in sunlight.
Wanted: honey from the wild hives on the cliffs above {place}. Hives are guarded by giant bees. Posted for {client}.
Lumber camp at {place} requires heartwood from a lightning-struck tree in the old forest. Only one such tree is known. {npc} can point the way.
Gather materials from a recently cleared astral space, {astral}, near {place}, before the remnants fade. Society inspector must be present.
Wanted: {count} bundles of moonmoss from the caves above {place}. Pick only the silver-tipped stalks. The rest is poisonous.
{client} needs fresh {monster} venom, extracted from a living specimen near {place}. Container provided. Gloves advised.
Gather the eggs of the cliff birds at {place} before the season ends. The birds will object.
Alchemist seeks {count} glowing beetles from the marsh near {place}. Live. Unharmed. Uneaten by you.
The temple at {place} needs fresh spring water from the mountain source, carried in blessed jars. Do not let the jars touch iron.
Collect salvageable monster parts from the battlefield at {place}: horns, scales, claws. Sort them. Bring the list.
Mushroom harvest at {place}. The good ones grow in the shade of trees that move. Watch the trees.
Gather {count} pounds of dragonroot for the healers at {place}. It grows only where monsters bleed.
Wanted: the pollen of a flower that blooms once a year at night near {place}. The night is in {days} days.
{client} needs blackwater clay from the delta near {place}. It sets like stone and sells like gold.
Salt crystals that hum, from the dry lake at {place}. The Magic Society pays per ounce.
Gather wild honey from the giant hives near {place}. Beekeeper's suit provided. Spare suit advised.
details: The plants grow in a clearing that is also the feeding ground of a nocturnal {monster}.
Harvesting correctly requires a DC 13 Wisdom (Survival or Medicine) check; on a failure, half the material is ruined.
The material is found only on a ledge reachable by a DC 14 Strength (Athletics) climb.
The harvest site belongs to a hermit who demands a share or a favour in exchange.
The quantities requested would strip the site bare, and a druid circle objects.
The materials must be packed in ice to stay fresh, and the nearest ice house is a day away.
The best patch is within a monster's hunting ground, and the monster hunts at the same time the plants bloom.
The plant must be cut with silver or it withers in an hour.
A DC 13 Intelligence (Nature) check tells the valuable variety from the common one.
The gathering site is a sacred grove, and the druid who tends it charges a toll.
The site is on a cliff face, and harvesting needs ropes and a steady hand.
Last year's harvesters left traps for rivals, and some are still set.
The material spoils fast and must be carried back within two days.
The harvest attracts insects that carry a mild fever.
A local family has always harvested here and expects to be asked.
complications: Pollen from the plants causes hallucinations; DC 12 Constitution save each hour or be poisoned.
A rival herbalist hires thugs to raid the team's camp and steal the harvest.
A late frost has killed most of the crop, leaving only a few patches in dangerous places.
The monster guarding the materials is protected by a local noble's hunting law.
The jars provided by the client are cracked and leak.
Gathering triggers an ancient ward that summons {count} guardian spirits.
A rival gatherer has already stripped half the patch.
The weather turns, ruining half the harvest.
The material turns out to be illegal in the city it's going to.
A noble claims the land and demands a share.
The material reacts badly to one team member's essence.
The client's price drops when the team returns, because the market has moved.
A monster has been feeding on the same plants and isn't willing to share.
The container breaks and the material starts to leak.
Someone poisons the patch the night before the harvest.
twists: The client intends to brew a poison from the gathered materials, not medicine.
The materials are rare because the last gatherers were killed, and the client has not mentioned it.
The site is sacred to a local church, and harvesting it is quietly forbidden.
The plants are seeds of an invasive magical weed that could choke a whole valley.
The client already has the materials and is testing whether the team is reliable for a bigger job.
The material is an ingredient for a cult ritual, not medicine.
Harvesting the plant wakes the ancient tree spirit it was feeding.
The client is collecting enough to corner the market and ruin the village that relies on it.
The plants are the only thing keeping a nearby monster population in check.
The material is an essence ingredient that nobody yet knows how to use.
The gathering site is the only thing holding shut a crack into an astral space.
A team member's essence reacts to the material and gains a new sense, briefly.
proof: The gathered materials in the required quantity and condition
The client's signed acceptance of the goods
Inspection by a Magic Society appraiser
The goods, weighed and checked by the client
A merchant's certificate of quality
Samples left with the Society for inspection

types.label: Patrol
notices: Patrol contract. Walk the road from {place} to the river ford and back each day for {days} days. Report any {monster} sightings.
Military order: supplement the watch on the eastern perimeter of {place}. Shifts at dawn and dusk. Report to {npc}.
The road wardens seek patrols between {place} and Greenstone. Bandit activity by {faction} has risen sharply.
{client} requests adventurers to patrol the vineyard boundary near {place} during the harvest. Thieves and beasts both suspected.
Patrol needed in the marsh channels near {place}. Ferrymen have seen {monster} under the water. Boats provided.
Society Notice: increased patrols are ordered around the astral space {astral} near {place} while it awaits clearance.
Night patrol of the Old City district bordering {place}. Lamplighters have refused to work since {count} of them disappeared.
We are just a few houses at {place}, and the soldiers do not come anymore. Walk our fields at night and let the {monster} know someone is watching.
Patrol the coast road between {place} and the next village for {days} days. Report anything odd. Fight anything odder.
Night patrol of {place}'s outer farms. Wolves, mostly. Probably wolves.
The Society needs a team to walk the ditches and dykes around {place} after the flood. Mark breaches. Kill what's in them.
Ride the border around {client}'s land for {days} days. Turn back trespassers politely. Report impolite ones.
Patrol the forest paths near {place}. Woodcutters have started hearing whistles that answer theirs.
Walk the city walls of {place} on the night shift. The guards are short-handed and short-tempered.
Patrol the river between {place} and the delta. Barges are vanishing. The river isn't saying where.
Patrol the market district of {place} during the festival. Pickpockets, drunks, and the occasional escaped monster.
Sweep the hills above {place} for signs of a surge. The Magic Society reads the signs. You go and look.
Patrol the pilgrim road to {place} during the holy week. Protect the faithful. Tolerate their singing.
Patrol the edge of the dead zone near {place}. Make sure nothing comes out. Or goes in.
Patrol the trade road through {place} and check every caravan's papers. Smugglers are using forged Society seals.
details: The patrol route crosses three villages, each with its own complaints and requests for the team.
A simple pattern emerges by the third day: the monsters only cross where the road meets the stream.
The previous patrol slacked off and left forged reports; the true danger is much worse than recorded.
Locals leave food and drink for the patrol, some of it laced with sleeping herbs by a thief.
The patrol area includes a stretch of ruined wall where {monster} nest during the day.
Weather turns foul for most of the patrol, with fog reducing visibility to thirty feet.
The patrol route passes a hermit who knows everything that moves in the area and wants company.
There is a cairn every mile, and someone has been rearranging the stones.
The route includes a ford that is only passable at low water.
The patrol overlaps with a noble's hunting party, which treats the team as servants.
A traveller on the route keeps passing the team, always going the other way.
The patrol includes a stop at a farm where the family insists on feeding everyone.
Two waystations on the route; one has been looted.
Monsters near the route have learned the patrol's timing.
A bell tower in the middle of the route can signal the whole area if anyone remembers how to ring it.
complications: Boredom sets in; each day without incident requires a DC 12 Wisdom save to stay alert.
A merchant demands the patrol escort him personally, threatening to complain to the Society.
The patrol stumbles on a crime in progress far outside its route.
Soldiers from the garrison resent the adventurers and refuse to share information.
A section of the route floods, forcing a dangerous detour.
One night the team finds the remains of another patrol that was never reported.
The team finds a body on the patrol route on the first night.
Rain makes the route twice as long.
A villager accuses the team of stealing livestock.
Another patrol is supposed to meet the team halfway and doesn't arrive.
Someone has set a decoy campfire to lure the team off the route.
A road agent tries to collect a toll from the patrol itself.
The patrol finds smugglers, and the smugglers have papers from the client.
An injured monster is found on the route, and it's very young.
Half the route is under a curse that makes everyone suspicious of each other.
twists: The patrol is meant to be seen, drawing attention away from a secret shipment moving elsewhere.
The bandits are local farmers driven to crime by unfair taxes.
The patrol route was designed to keep adventurers away from a smuggling tunnel.
The missing lamplighters were taken by something that hunts by light.
The garrison commander wants the patrol to fail so he can justify more funding.
The patrol was arranged to keep the team away from a crime elsewhere.
The trouble on the route comes from a new astral space that keeps moving its door.
The team discovers the previous patrol was killed and replaced by impostors.
The hermit is a retired Gold-rank adventurer hiding from her past.
The disappearing barges are being sunk deliberately to hide something on the riverbed.
The patrol route crosses a ley line, and something is feeding on it.
The forged Society seals were made inside the Society.
proof: A daily log signed by a local authority
Completion of the full patrol period without abandoning the route
Reports of any incidents with evidence
A full patrol log, signed by each waystation keeper
Witness accounts of anything found or fought
The patrol badge returned with its route marks

types.label: Survey
notices: The Adventure Society requires a survey of monster populations in the forest east of {place}. Count the {monster}, record their dens and avoid unnecessary kills.
Survey contract. Chart the new course of the river near {place} after last month's floods. Note safe crossings and hazards. Complete within {days} days. Posted for {client}.
{client} needs an accurate survey of farmland near {place} for a boundary dispute. Bring a measuring chain and patience.
The Magic Society requests a mana flow survey of the hills around {place}. Instruments provided by {npc}. Do not drop them.
Survey needed of the road from {place} to the coast. Bridges, inns, dangers and monster dens must be marked. {days} days permitted.
Cartographers' guild seeks surveyors for the marsh region beyond {place}. {monster} territory must be noted precisely.
Inspect and report on the condition of the ward stones surrounding {place}. Several are reported cracked. Contact {npc}.
Survey team requested for the cliffs above {place}, where a portal to {astral} may soon open. Record any signs.
Survey the proposed route for a new road from {place} to the quarry. Note terrain, water, monsters, and anything that might fall on a road.
{client} intends to buy land near {place}. Survey it before he does. Discretion, please.
Magic Society survey: measure the ambient magic at {count} points around {place}. Instruments provided. Instruments fragile.
Count the {monster} population around {place} for the Society's records. Don't thin it. Just count it.
Survey the coastline south of {place} for a possible new harbour. Check depths, rocks and anything that lives in the water.
Survey the ruins of the old fort at {place} for repair. A mason comes with you. He is afraid of heights.
Re-survey the boundary between two estates near {place}. The old markers have been moved. By someone.
Map the springs near {place} for the water-sellers' guild. Mark which are clean. Mark which glow.
Survey the damage after the storm at {place}. Count homes, boats, livestock, and the dead.
Survey a new astral portal near {place}: entrance only, no further. Note any monsters that come out.
Survey the old mine at {place} for reopening. It was closed for a reason nobody wrote down.
Survey the herds of wild horses on the plains near {place}. The steppe clans may object.
details: The terrain is rough; covering it fully requires a DC 13 Wisdom (Survival) check each day or lose a day.
The monster population has grown far beyond earlier counts; something is drawing them in.
The measuring instruments are sensitive to magic and give false readings near ruins.
A hermit lives in the survey area and objects to strangers on his land.
Landmarks on the old maps have been moved or destroyed.
Half the ward stones are fine; the cracked ones are all on the side facing the marsh.
The instruments behave oddly near a certain hill, which is the point of the survey.
The land has three claimants, and each tries to bribe the surveyors.
The survey needs a clear view from a hilltop held by monsters.
The old maps are a hundred years out of date and wrong about a river.
Locals don't know the survey is happening and treat the team as spies.
A DC 13 Intelligence check reads the old boundary markers correctly.
The terrain is dangerous: sinkholes, loose rocks or bog.
The survey must be finished before the client's buyers arrive.
A previous survey team left notes that disagree with everything they find.
complications: Two noble families each try to bribe the team for a favourable survey.
A territorial {monster} stalks the team for most of the survey.
The survey area includes a sinkhole that opens beneath the team; DC 14 Dexterity save or fall 20 feet.
Pages of the team's notes go missing, stolen by an interested party.
The instruments break on the second day and must be repaired or improvised.
The weather prevents accurate readings for several days.
A landowner meets the team with dogs and a crossbow.
The instruments are damaged on the first day.
The mason, or scholar, or guide, falls ill.
The survey finds something the client clearly does not want recorded.
A rival surveyor is producing a different map for the same client.
The weather prevents any accurate measurement for two days.
The survey route runs straight through a cult's meeting place.
Local spirits object to being measured.
Someone tampers with the team's notes overnight.
twists: The ward stones were cracked on purpose by someone who wants the town undefended.
The survey reveals the land belongs to a different family than everyone believed.
The monster increase is caused by an unregistered astral space about to burst.
The client wants the survey to fail so they can delay a road that would ruin their business.
The cartographers' guild will sell the survey to {faction} for smuggling routes.
The survey finds a deposit of something valuable, and now everyone wants the land.
The land is a burial ground for a people who still live nearby.
The magic readings show an astral space is forming slowly underground.
The client wants to flood the valley, and a village is in the way.
The moved boundary markers were moved back to where they belong.
The old mine was closed because the miners dug into something alive.
The survey proves a famous family's claim to their land is a forgery.
proof: A complete survey map and written log
Instrument readings submitted to the Magic Society
Acceptance of the report by the Society's survey clerk
The completed survey, signed and dated
Instrument readings, sealed in the Magic Society's case
A map copied into the Society's records

types.label: Monster Surge
notices: SURGE ALERT. Monsters are pouring out of {astral} near {place}. All available Iron and Bronze teams report immediately.
Society Emergency Contract: a monster surge has struck {place}. Hold the line against the {monster}, protect civilians, and await reinforcements.
Military order: all licensed adventurers within a day's ride of {place} are called to assist against a surge of {monster}. Report to {npc}.
Surge response. {count} {monster} have overrun the outlying farms of {place}. Evacuate survivors and drive them back.
they came out of the ground at {place} like ants. so many. the town is barricaded. {monster}, hundreds of them. please send anyone who can fight.
Surge clean-up contract. The main surge at {place} is broken, but scattered {monster} remain in the fields. Clear them within {days} days.
{client} begs the Society to protect her mill at {place} from the surge. It holds a winter of grain for three villages.
Society Notice: possible surge brewing at {astral} near {place}. Teams are to stand watch and engage if the portal ruptures.
SURGE WARNING. The Magic Society predicts a monster surge near {place} within {days} days. All available teams report to the duty clerk.
Surge response: {monster} pouring out of the hills near {place}. Hold the line at the river until reinforcements arrive.
A surge has broken the defences at {place}. Evacuate the outlying farms, then hold the gate.
The Society needs teams to find and kill the surge leader near {place}. Kill the leader and the rest scatter.
Post-surge sweep: clear the stragglers from the fields around {place} so the farmers can return.
Surge scouting: count the monsters massing in the valley above {place}. Do not engage. Do not be seen.
Help needed to build barricades at {place} before the surge. Strong backs and stronger nerves.
Surge relief: carry supplies to the cut-off village at {place}, through the surge.
The surge at {place} has a pattern the Magic Society doesn't understand. Get them a live specimen.
Hunt the {count} surge monsters that slipped past the line at {place} and are heading for the farms.
Guard the Magic Society team trying to read the surge's source near {place}. They won't stop working. You won't stop fighting.
Surge aftermath: the dead at {place} need burying before nightfall. Some are not staying dead.
details: The surge is mostly weak creatures, but every third wave includes a stronger leader.
Monsters are drawn to light and noise; a quiet, dark defence holds better.
Refugees crowd the road out of town, slowing reinforcements to a crawl.
The local garrison is brave but undertrained and breaks if its sergeant falls.
The monsters attack in waves roughly an hour apart, giving time for brief rests.
A Gold-rank team is on its way but will not arrive for a day.
The surge leader is a {monster} a full rank above the rest, and it stays at the back.
The monsters come in waves, about an hour apart, each larger than the last.
The surge follows the river, and the bridges are the choke points.
Some monsters carry essence-bright cores visible at night, making them easy to spot and tempting to chase.
The surge is driving every animal in the region ahead of it, and stampedes come first.
The local militia has fled, leaving their armoury unlocked.
A Magic Society ward line half-works; monsters crossing it are slowed but not stopped.
The surge's source is a cluster of new astral spaces opening in a ring.
A natural fortification, an old hill fort, could hold if anyone can reach it.
complications: A large monster smashes through a barricade, and the gap must be held for {count} rounds.
The team is ordered to protect a wealthy district while a poorer one burns.
Monster blood is caustic; each melee hit requires a DC 12 Dexterity save or take 2d6 acid damage.
Healing supplies run out by the second wave.
A panicked mob blocks the main street while monsters close in.
A Society official tries to take credit for the defence and gives contradictory orders.
A noble refuses to leave his manor and demands protection.
Panicking refugees block the only road.
The surge splits in two, and the team has to choose which side to hold.
A second team is out of position, and the line has a gap.
Night falls and the monsters see better than the defenders.
A Society officer gives orders that will get people killed.
Supply wagons are overrun, and arrows run short.
The monsters start digging under the barricades.
One of the defenders is secretly feeding information to a cult.
twists: The surge was triggered on purpose by {faction} to cover a theft in the confusion.
The portal was weakened by a negligent Society team that never reported their failure.
The monsters are fleeing something even more dangerous inside the space.
A noble paid to delay the Society's response so the surge would destroy a rival's property.
One of the monsters carries a human-made collar, suggesting someone controls them.
The surge was triggered deliberately by a cult opening astral spaces.
The surge leader is not a monster but a corrupted adventurer.
The surge is heading somewhere specific, and it isn't the town.
A noble house is profiting from the surge by buying abandoned land.
Killing the surge leader makes things worse; it was holding the others back.
The monsters are fleeing an astral being whose attention has turned to this world.
The Magic Society's prediction was late on purpose, so a rival director would look bad.
proof: Monster cores or bodies collected during the defence
Survival of the defended area, confirmed by local officials
A Society commander's sign-off on the team's participation
Surge leader's core, presented at the counter
The Society commander's report on the team's part in the defence
Cores from the fallen, counted by the duty clerk

types.label: Cult Raid
notices: Society Contract: a cult calling itself {faction} has been spotted performing rituals near {place}. Disrupt their activities and bring members to justice.
Raid order. The church of {place} has identified a hidden shrine of {faction} beneath an old granary. Strike at dawn.
Cultists of {faction} have been kidnapping travellers on the road to {place}. Find their lair and free the captives.
The Magic Society reports forbidden magic used near {place}. Suspect {faction}. Recover any texts intact for study.
my sister joined the people in grey robes at {place}. she does not know me anymore. they call themselves {faction}. please bring her back before the next full moon.
Military order: assault the {faction} compound outside {place}. Take prisoners for interrogation. Burn the rest.
{client} believes their son has fallen in with {faction} near {place} and wants him returned unharmed. Discretion beyond all else.
Investigate and destroy the cult of {faction}, whose members have been seen summoning {monster} in the hills above {place}.
The Society has reason to believe a cult cell meets in {place}. Find it. Confirm it. Report before acting.
Strange symbols painted on doors in {place}. The Church of Truth wants them read and the painters found.
Cult activity suspected at the old shrine near {place}. Investigate. Do not touch the altar.
Missing children in {place}, and a cult's mark on the wall where they were last seen. Find them.
A recruit has escaped a cult near {place} and wants out of the city. Protect her until she testifies.
Raid a known cult hideout in {place}. The Church of Justice will follow with chains. Get there first.
{client} suspects his son has joined a cult in {place}. Bring him home, sane if possible.
Someone in {place} is buying rare reagents used in forbidden rituals. Follow the purchases.
Cult hunters wanted for a sweep of {place}'s sewers. Bring light. Bring friends.
A cult preacher is drawing crowds in the market at {place}. Find out who he answers to.
Infiltrate the new mentoring circle in {place}. It is probably harmless. Probably.
Burn out the cult nest at {place}. The Society has confirmation and authority. Kill only if you must.
details: The cult has {count} members, most of them desperate villagers led by one charismatic leader.
The cult's hideout is a series of tunnels beneath a ruined manor with only two exits.
The cultists believe their ritual will end a drought, and some have truly seen rain follow it.
The cult leader is Bronze rank with powerful dark essence abilities and a fanatical bodyguard.
A DC 14 Charisma (Deception) check lets a disguised party member infiltrate a meeting.
The cult's ritual requires a sacrifice at the next new moon, and they already have a captive.
The cult uses a bakery as a front, and the bread is good, which is the problem.
Members recognise each other by a ring worn on the left little finger.
The cult meets on the night of each new moon, and the next is in {days} days.
A Magic Society researcher has been feeding the cult information without realising.
The cult has a safehouse in every district, and each knows only the next.
The cult's leader is a respected figure in {place} and has never been seen at a meeting.
Cult members carry a small vial that kills them if they are captured.
A former member is willing to talk but only to a priest.
The cult has a defector in its ranks, already reporting to someone else.
complications: Many cultists are local farmers with families, and the town will turn on anyone who kills them.
The cult leader has a hostage and will kill them if the team attacks directly.

Courier required for diplomatic correspondence to the lord of {place}. Must be well-mannered and presentable. Sent on behalf of {client}.
Military dispatch: carry orders to the outpost at {place}. Roads may be watched by {faction}. Memorise and destroy if captured.
Message for my son, a soldier stationed at {place}. I have not heard from him in months. Please give it to him and tell me he is well. His name is {npc}.
{client} begs the favour of gentle couriers to deliver a letter of the most tender nature to a lady in {place}. Reply eagerly awaited.
Society Notice: carry the summons to {npc} at {place}, who is required to appear before the license tribunal within {days} days.
Carry a warning to {place}: {monster} are moving toward them from the south. Ride fast.
The Magic Society needs a research report delivered to a colleague in {place}. Do not let it get wet. The ink runs. Recipient: {npc}.
Deliver a sealed message to {npc} at {place}. Must be read aloud in their presence. Reply required.
{client} needs a letter carried to {place} faster than the post. Pay doubles if it arrives before {days} days.
Carry a summons from the magistrate to a man in {place} who does not want to be summoned.
Deliver an apology to {place}. It is very long, and the recipient must hear all of it.
Get word to the farms near {place} that the surge is coming. Every farm. Before nightfall.
Deliver a marriage proposal to a family in {place}. Wait for the answer. Do not react to the answer.
Carry the news of a death to the family at {place}. Gently. They don't know yet.
Find {npc}, somewhere in the hills near {place}, and tell them their mother is dying.

Deliver a challenge to a duel on behalf of {client}. The recipient is a Silver-ranker. Run afterwards.
Deliver the town's petition to the duke's steward at {place}. It has six hundred signatures and one fake.

The message carries a seal that burns if tampered with.

The answer has to come back in a day, and the road takes two.
The message was copied by someone at an inn the night before.
The recipient wants to reply in person and comes back with the team.
The recipient is dead, and their killer is reading their mail.
A noble on the road insists on knowing the business of anyone passing.

The recipient is the client's secret child.

The team carries a love letter between two feuding houses.

Reading the message aloud triggers a spell bound into the paper.

Tournament security at {place}. Watch for cheats, poisoners and overzealous fans. Report to {npc}.

Guard the duel at {place} and make sure only one person dies. The right one.
Watch the crowd at the public execution in {place}. The condemned has friends.
Guard the Magic Society exhibition of rare essences at {place}. Look at nothing. Touch less.
Protect the visiting envoy during the feast at {place}. Taste nothing. Trust no one.
The festival of lanterns at {place} needs fire-watchers. Bring buckets. Bring patience.
Guard the rank assessment trials at {place}. Candidates sometimes cheat. Families sometimes help.
Security for a funeral at {place}. The widow has enemies and the deceased owed money to all of them.

The guest list includes two rivals who have sworn to kill each other on sight.

A suspicious package is found under the stage an hour before the main event.

The venue has a single entrance and a lot of windows.

The event's centrepiece is a gift worth more than the venue.

A noble's bodyguard and the team's ranks are equal, and he wants to prove he's better.
complications: An assassination attempt happens in the middle of a dance.
A sudden storm forces the event indoors into a building too small for the crowd.
Drunk guests pick fights with the guards to show off.
The client insists that guards stay invisible, leaving them far from where they are needed.
A fire breaks out in the kitchens at the height of the event.
A guest collapses from poison and the host demands the team find the culprit before anyone leaves.
A fight breaks out between two guests over an old insult.

A guest collapses, and everyone assumes poison.
The host's dog bites a duke.
A gate-crasher claims to be the host's long-lost brother.
The event runs past midnight and the team's contract ends at midnight.
A rival team arrives, hired by a different guest.

The guest of honour is late, and the delay sets everyone on edge.

The threats came from inside the host's family.
A thief uses the commotion to rob the host's vault during the speeches.

The festival's sacred bonfire is meant to cover a ritual by {faction}.

The real target is one of the guards.
The event is cover for a secret meeting between two factions.
A cultist means to make a public declaration during the event.

The sewers under {place} are crawling with {monster}. The city requires a thorough cleansing. Bring boots.

Society Iron-rank contract: exterminate a nest of {count} {monster} in the abandoned watermill near {place}.
{client} regrets that a colony of {monster} has taken up residence in the east wing near {place}. Removal is required before the guests arrive.
Clear the spider nests from the old mine at {place} so the workers can return. Burn the egg sacs. {npc} will pay on completion.
The bats in the bell tower of {place} have become something worse. The bells have not rung in a month. Help. Signed, {client}.

Exterminate the {monster} infesting the cellars beneath {place}. All of them. Every last one. Check twice.

Clear the sewers under {place} of {monster}. They've started coming up through the drains.
The orchard at {place} is overrun with {monster}. Kill them before they kill the trees.
Burn out the {monster} nest in the old barn at {place}. Owner has given permission. Owner has also left town.
The mine at {place} has been taken by {monster}. The miners want their tools back. And the mine.
Clear the {monster} from the bell tower at {place} before the festival. The bells must ring.
The {monster} in the reed beds at {place} are breeding fast. Kill them all before spring.

Exterminate the {monster} in the temple catacombs at {place}. Respect the dead. The monsters don't.

The monsters lay eggs in anything soft, including clothing.
Some of the creatures carry spirit coins and other shiny things in their nests.

my husband died in the mine at {place}. they say it is too dangerous to go back. i just want to bury him. his name was {npc}.
